item.description:
Portside now keeps itself current — and this first self-updating build
also delivers everything landed since 0.2.0: tabs, a real terminal, and a
window that remembers your working day.

### What's new

- A standard Mac installation: download `Portside-0.3.0.dmg`, open it, and
  follow the visible Portside-to-Applications arrow. One signed, notarized disk
  image serves trial installs, purchases, and later Sparkle updates; there is no
  customer-facing zip or installer package.
- Self-updating via Sparkle (decision 0057): the app checks
  getportside.com's feed and installs new versions in place, then
  relaunches. No check runs before the one-time consent prompt is
  answered, and "Check for Updates…" under About asks explicitly at any
  time. These notes appear in the update dialog itself.
- Tabs in both panes: each side keeps its own ordered tabs with their
  folders and sort; background tabs stay live but are never the target
  of an operation, and a tab holding an open dialog or a running
  transfer refuses to close.
- The command bar expands into a real terminal — a login shell in a
  PTY, one per tab, toggled with ⌃`. It follows the active pane's
  folder while the shell is idle, dev servers and ssh sessions keep
  running, and ⌘-clicked http(s) links open in your browser.
- Permanent deletion as its own explicit command (⌥F8 / ⌥⌘⌫) beside
  Trash-only F8, and ⌘Z "Undo Move to Trash" brings the last trashed
  batch back.
- Overwrite in a conflict is now permanent — this reverses 0.2.0's
  behaviour. The replacement is copied in full and swapped into place
  atomically, and the displaced item is then deleted for good, never to
  the Trash; the confirmation dialog says exactly that before you
  agree. (It also means volumes without a Trash can overwrite.)
- Favorites can be renamed and reordered in the sidebar.
- The workspace survives relaunch: tabs, sorts, the active tab, the
  hidden-items toggle, and the window's size and position all return.
  The Settings window (⌘,) chooses startup behaviour — reopen last
  workspace or start fresh in a chosen folder — and System/Light/Dark
  appearance.
- Typed navigation: Go to Folder (⇧⌘G) and in-place path editing
  (⌘L or double-click the path).
- Copy Path (⌥⌘C) and Copy Name, selection tools (deselect all,
  invert, select by pattern), volume eject from the volume menus,
  free space in each pane's footer, and a keyboard-shortcuts
  reference (⇧⌘/).

### Known limitations

- Builds before 0.3.0 predate the updater and cannot update in place;
  they are superseded by one final manual DMG download.
- The published feed carries the latest release only (deferred in
  decision 0057 with its consequences recorded there).
- Name collisions offer Keep or Overwrite per item, and folders merge —
  but keep-both/rename-on-conflict is still not available.
- Once a cross-volume move has committed an item at the destination,
  that item can no longer be cancelled; cancellation between items and
  mid-copy still works.
- No SFTP or other remote protocols. No deep search.
